preceding_messages.text: I adopt the fourteen-day overlap, the bridging-line rule, and the bold "BRIDGE PENDING" header annotation verbatim; they make the replacement window auditable without reopening the two-week persistence gate. For the reporting question your audit-trail requirement implies but has not yet regulated, every weekly bulletin will carry a SHA-256 hash of the compiled dataset, and a permanent public-appendix section—accessible to any resident by request—where horizon-sketch scans, elevation-survey records, bridging lines, and errata are filed in serial-number order alongside the bound logbook. The concrete failure this guards against: a well-meaning volunteer "corrects" a transcription slip (18.4 → 18.5 °C) directly in the compiled file without entering an erratum line, so the archived logbook and eleven successive printed bulletins diverge by 0.1 °C, and when a resident in year two pulls the bound logbook to verify a cooling trend the quiet discrepancy reads as fabrication and strips the project of its public-credibility anchor. I therefore mandate that any post-compilation edit requires a two-initials erratum entry in the bound logbook and a superseding bulletin issued within five working days, printed with the prior hash struck through and the revised hash alongside, so the audit trail and the bulletin can never silently desynchronize.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the SHA-256 hash sealing, the two-initials erratum mandate, and the five-day superseding-bulletin-with-struck-through-prior-hash rule verbatim; they make the audit trail tamper-evident without reopening the weekly comparison tolerances. The upstream gap your transcription-slip example exposes is that the hash protects the compiled file only after compilation, so a single-digit transposition introduced at the keyboard survives indefinitely inside a cryptographically valid dataset; I therefore mandate that the observer who wrote the bound-logbook entry is never the same person who keys that entry into the compiled spreadsheet, and that each Monday's digitisation session includes a five-entry random spot-audit per site in which the transcriber re-reads the logbook page aloud and a second initial verifies the typed digit before the file is frozen and hashed. The concrete failure this closes: at Site 3's 02:00 graduated-cylinder read, a tired volunteer logs −2.6 °C, the transcriber's tired fingers enter −2.9 °C, and because the 0.3 °C delta sits below both your ±0.5 °C weekly temperature tolerance and the ±0.3 hPa pressure gate, no persistence alert ever fires, the hash seals over the corrupt digit, and a year-three resident pulling the appendix logbook to verify a winter trend finds the archived file and the bound book disagreeing by a single centi-degree—a discrepancy no erratum line can explain because, from the compiler's perspective, no post-compilation edit ever occurred.

target.speaker: X
target.text: I adopt the observer/transcriber separation and the five-entry Monday spot-audit verbatim; they close the keyboard-transposition hole at its source rather than relying on the hash to detect corruption it cannot. For the graduated-cylinder winter read specifically, I require that any observer whose initials have not yet appeared on three supervised 02:00 readings—each with the certifier's concurrent reading and a delta ≤ 0.1 mm water-equivalent—may not log frozen-precipitation entries independently until that threshold is met. The failure this prevents: a first-week volunteer reads the meniscus apex rather than the base, introducing a +0.3 mm/event bias that over four winter events produces a +1.2 mm seasonal overcount—below the ±2 mm weekly precipitation comparison tolerance I now mandate—so no persistence alert fires, the instrument is perfectly healthy at every monthly cross-check, and a year-three appendix audit surfaces a twelve-millimetre phantom accumulation attributable to no serial number, no bridging line, and no post-compilation edit. I therefore print the certifier's initials alongside the volunteer's on every graduated-cylinder entry until the three-reading threshold is cleared, and any site whose 02:00 entries lack that pairing for more than one week triggers the same formal review as the thirty-percent zero-speed wind rule.
